finding.claim: Uploaded .xml files are accepted with no content inspection and are served with application/xml. An attacker who can upload a file through a form or media field can store an XHTML-namespace XML document with inline <script>. If the upload is publicly reachable from the web root, a victim who opens that URL runs the script in the site origin (stored XSS). Only SVG uploads are scanned; the same sanitizer exists for SVG, so .xml is an inconsistent gap.
finding.source: Multipart upload from an unauthenticated or low-privilege visitor on any form/media field that does not restrict accept types (client filename ending in .xml, client media type application/xml).
finding.sink: Stored file at the upload destination, later served by the web server as application/xml (mime.yaml / media.yaml:103-106), rendered by the browser in the site origin.

trace.note: validateUpload(): only checks filename via Utils::checkFilename and calls FormFlashFile::checkXss() on the upload.
checkXss() short-circuits unless the client media type contains 'svg'; .xml gets no scan.
checkUploadedFile() builds metadata with the browser-supplied client filename and media type.
Extension is checked only for membership in media.types; xml is allowed.
Browser-supplied mime is used (not sniffed); application/xml maps to ['xml'], so the extension/mime consistency check passes.
xml is declared as an allowed media type, mime application/xml.
uploads_dangerous_extensions omits xml (lists php, phtml, html, htm, shtml, js, svg-related only via sanitize_svg, etc.).
xml is in xss_dangerous_tags, so the project knows XML is an XSS vector, but that scan applies only to page content, not uploads.

finding.guards_checked: Filename traversal and separators (Utils::checkFilename, Utils.php:1022-1039) - pass; dangerous-extension list - xml not blocked; media.types allowlist - xml allowed; client mime trusted but only for extension consistency - passes for xml; SVG sanitizer (Security.php:57-97) - applies only to svg; FormFlashFile::checkXss - svg only. Not verified: the form field 'accept' restriction and destination (both live outside this repo), and whether the destination is web-accessible (no .htaccess or nginx config in repo). Severity depends on those; reported as plausible, not confirmed.
